summary: R. Ramanujachari worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Annamalai University (attested 1938–1940) and as editor of the Journal of the Annamalai University (attested 1950).

R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) earned a master's in chemistry from the University of Mysore. An Indologist, he taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984) and served as President of the Indian Music Congress.
R. T. Vyas is an Indologist who served as General Editor of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1988) and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara from 1993 to 1994.

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Annamalai University and Madras Sanskrit College. His posts included University of Madras (~1968–1984) and Honorary Professor at Adyar Library and Research Centre (1994–2000).

R. Venkatraman is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, and later served there as Reader (attested 1990).

Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School and University College London. Active in philosophy, he founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.
Rachael Wiseman studied at the University of York and works in philosophy. She served as a lecturer at the University of Liverpool (~2013).

Rachel H. Pang earned her PhD from the University of Virginia. Specializing in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, she served as Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

Rachelle M. Scott completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay. A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, she held a post at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).
Radha Burnier (1923–2013) studied at Kalakshetra and Banaras Hindu University. Working in Indology and philosophy, she served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre from ~1959 to 1980.

Radha Krishna Choudhary (1921–1985) studied at Tej Narayan Banaili College and Patna University. An Indology and history scholar, he founded the Kashi Prasad Jaiswal Archaeological Museum and taught at Ganesh Dutt College and Tilka Manjhi Bhagalpur University (1974–1984).

Radha Kumud Mukherjee (1884–1963) studied at the University of Calcutta. An Indologist and historian, he held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1917) and Maharaja's College, University of Mysore (~1917–1921) as Head of the Department of History.

Radhika Herzberger completed her PhD at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal in 1982. A scholar of Indology and philosophy, she served as Director of Rishi Valley School from ~1980 to 2012.

Radoslav Katičić (1930–2019) studied at the University of Zagreb. Working in linguistics and Indology, he held posts at the University of Vienna (~1977–1998) and the Croatian Academy of Sciences and Arts (~1973–2019).

Rafal Stepien earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü and Bernard Faure. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, he was an Academic Visitor at Wadham College (2012–2013) and an Exchange Scholar at Harvard University (attested 2015).
Rafał Jan Felbur is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a PhD candidate at Stanford University, where he studied under Paul Harrison, John R. McRae, and Luis Oscar Gómez.
Raffaele Catà studied philosophy and Indology at the University of Bologna, completing his laurea in 2011–2012 under supervisor Manlio Iofrida and co-supervisor Saverio Marchignoli.

Raffaele Torella studied under Raniero Gnoli. A scholar of Indology and philosophy, he was a faculty member at the University of Rome (~1976–2020) and later held a professorship at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2022).
Raffaello Orlando is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University in 1981 under the supervision of Denis Twitchett.

Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. Active in philosophy and religious studies, he taught at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and visited IIM Ahmedabad (attested 2010).
